author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Rhode Island Department of Health advised the public Monday to avoid contact with Lower Melville Pond in Portsmouth because of a harmful algae bloom, Coastal ABC reported. The warning covers swimming, fishing and boating in the pond while the bloom is present.

Health officials said cyanobacteria can produce toxins that harm people and animals. Residents were urged not to drink the water, eat fish caught there or allow pets to enter it. Anyone who comes into contact with the pond should rinse off, and pets should be washed with clean water.

RIDOH lifted a separate algae-related advisory for Georgiaville Pond in Smithfield. The change does not apply to Lower Melville Pond, where the department’s current guidance remains to avoid contact until officials determine conditions are safe.
RIDOH’s distinction between the two ponds means residents should check the exact waterbody named in any advisory before returning to recreational use.
dek: RIDOH issued an advisory for Lower Melville Pond in Portsmouth because of a harmful algae bloom and urged people to keep pets away from the water.
headline: Rhode Island health officials warn against contact with Lower Melville Pond
